::: {#exr-racket-tree}
#### A binary tree in Racket

In Racket, store the empty tree (@def-binary-tree) as `'()`,
and $\operatorname{node}(x, L, R)$ as the list `(list x L R)` of its label and its two subtrees.
The binary tree $B$ of @exm-binary-tree is then

```racket
(define B
  '(m (f (c () ())
         (h () (j () ())))
      (t (r (p () ()) ())
         (w () ()))))
```

`(second L)` and `(third L)` return the second and the third element of a list `L`.
What does `(first (second (third B)))` return?

:::
